accepted_prompt: Do you approve locking immediate access revocation, resumable-pending deletion, and destination-specific removal guidance now, while leaving deletion-receipt duration for a documented legal-policy review?

access_revocation.rule: Revoke CTRL access and active credentials before destructive erasure work begins.

partial_completion.rule: Any mandatory target without valid completion proof leaves the request in resumable_pending. Partial completion must never return success.

customer_controlled_copies.rule: For every known exported copy, name the destination and give one specific removal action. Never imply CTRL can recall a copy it does not control.

retained_deletion_receipt.rule: No retention duration or lawful basis is inferred from this approval. Runtime execution remains held until that policy is documented and approved.

decision_record.title: Whole-Brain erasure interaction and completion policy
decision_record.decision: CTRL will revoke access first, treat incomplete erasure as resumable pending rather than success, and give destination-specific removal guidance for customer-controlled copies, while deletion-receipt retention remains separately unbound.
rationale: Immediate access revocation contains further exposure before slower local, provider or retention work finishes.
Returning success alongside deletion errors would create a false and consequential privacy claim.
A generic warning about external copies is not useful enough; the customer needs to know where each copy went and what to do there.
Current ICO guidance does not prescribe a universal retention period, so receipt duration must come from a documented purpose and policy rather than an engineering guess.

alternatives.route: Return success after best-effort deletion and include an error list
alternatives.why_rejected: The headline state would be false whenever any mandatory target failed.

alternatives.route: Treat every incomplete target as a terminal hard failure
alternatives.why_rejected: Provider and retention work can be asynchronous and recoverable; a resumable state preserves honesty without discarding progress.
It transfers cognitive work to the customer and does not help them finish the deletion.

decision_record.dissent: Resumable deletion creates an operational obligation to retry and expose status safely. Revoking access first also means the completion receipt needs a secure delivery path that does not restore product access.
decision_record.tradeoffs: Some erasure requests will remain visibly pending instead of appearing instant. CTRL accepts the orchestration and status-design burden in exchange for an honest privacy promise.

assumptions.assumption: CTRL can discover every material export destination from durable export or processing receipts.
assumptions.flip_rule: Reopen the guidance design if a deletion can encounter an untraceable material destination.

assumptions.assumption: A secure content-free status channel can remain available after product access is revoked.
assumptions.flip_rule: Reopen the access-first sequence if verified implementation evidence shows status delivery requires restoring access to personal Brain data.

revisit.trigger: Verified implementation cannot safely deliver deletion status after access revocation, a material export destination cannot be traced, or legal review requires different completion or retention behavior.
revisit.signal_source: Versioned erasure execution proof, export-receipt coverage audit, customer comprehension test or documented legal review
revisit.action_when_fired: Set this decision to review_due and prepare a bounded keep, supersede or reverse decision without weakening current fail-closed behavior.
